newsitem.title: FRANCE: French left gains ground in election-poll.
newsitem.headline: French left gains ground in election-poll.

text.p: Following are the results of an opinion poll of voters' intentions ahead of the May 25/June 1 French parliamentary election.
The telephone poll of 1,000 adults aged 18 and over was conducted by SOFRES on May 2 and 3 for Monday's Le Figaro newspaper and made public on May 4:
Projected seats in the National Assembly
In the previous parliament, the Communists held 22 seats, the Socialists and their left-wing allies 63 while the UDF/RPR and allies had 470.

Sofres said 19 percent of those surveyed did not say how they would vote. In the survey, 65 percent said their party choice was definite, while 35 percent said they could still change their voting plans.

In the last poll Sofres conducted on April 25 and 26, it found that 2.5 percent supported the extreme left, nine percent favoured the Communists, 28 percent backed the Socialists and 1.5 percent other leftist groups, five percent would vote for ecologist candidates, 35 percent were supporters of the RPR/UDF and five percent of other right-wing parties while the Front National had the backing of 14 percent.
The new Sofres poll showed that the left would win a total of 262 seats and the centre-right 291 from among the 555 in metropolitan France.
The same Sofres poll conducted a week ago gave the left 225 seats and the centre-right 329 seats.
An IFOP poll released on Saturday first showed the rise in pro-left wing vote. It suggested the left would take between 255 and 285 seats and the centre-right between 269 and 299 seats.
